newsitem.title: UK: British economic growth revised upward.
newsitem.headline: British economic growth revised upward.

text.p: The British economy grew more quickly than originally reported in the last two quarters and growth in 1994 and 1995 was also revised upward, according to official data published Friday.

Economists said the figures suggested there was less spare capacity in the economy than previously thought and provided further evidence that interest rates would need to rise to prevent surging demand from pushing up inflation.
The Office for National Statistics said gross domestic product grew by 0.9 percent in the first quarter of this year, while the annual growth rate was revised to 3.1 percent from 3.0 percent.
Growth in the fourth quarter of 1996 was raised to 2.9 percent year-on-year from the 2.6 percent originally reported.
The statistics office said latest estimates showed the economy had grown by a robust 4.5 percent in 1994, well above the 4.0 percent last reported, and by 2.8 percent in 1995, instead of 2.5 percent.
